questions.prompt: A workflow fans out over 400 files and each agent returns a long summary. Where does the summary of the 40th file live while the remaining agents are still running?
options: In a variable inside the workflow script, outside Claude's context window
In Claude's context window, where the next decision can read it
In the agent team's shared task list
Appended to the session transcript, which the script reads back
questions.explanation: The runtime executes the script in an isolated environment and keeps intermediate results in script variables, which is the whole reason a workflow can scale past what one window holds. The first wrong option is the instinct carried over from subagents — there, results do land in the window, and that is exactly the constraint a workflow removes. Agent teams use a shared task list, which is for tasks rather than agent outputs, and the transcript is a record of what was said, not a working store the script reads.

questions.prompt: A CI job runs `claude -p "ultracode: audit every route handler"`. The audit runs turn by turn and no workflow starts. Why?
options: The keyword only opts in from a prompt a human typed; a `-p` prompt does not trigger it
Workflows are unavailable in non-interactive mode, so Claude Code stripped the keyword
The keyword has to be the first character of the prompt, and a quote preceded it
The workflow needs to be saved as a command before the keyword can launch it
questions.explanation: The docs list the routes that count as human input — the interactive prompt, an IDE panel, a Remote Control client, an SDK app that stamps the input as human — and `-p` is explicitly not one of them; neither is a scheduled task prompt or a relayed webhook. The unavailable-in-`-p` option is the tempting one because workflows are indeed young, but the pages state they run in non-interactive mode and in the Agent SDK. The quote has nothing to do with it, and a workflow does not need saving before it can run — saving is for reuse.

questions.prompt: Your workflow script needs to read `.tool-versions` and branch on its contents. What does the script do?
options: Give an agent the job of reading the file and returning the value, because the script itself has no filesystem access
`import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'` inside the script body
Read the value with a top-level `await fetch('file://.tool-versions')`
Nothing — the script must ask the user for the value, because runs take no input
questions.explanation: The workflow coordinates; agents read, write, and run commands. The first wrong option is the one most developers reach for, and it fails twice: the runtime rejects a script containing `import()` before the run even starts, and there is no filesystem for the script to use. Fetching a `file://` URL is not part of the documented script surface and runs into the same missing-access wall. The last option confuses the run's inability to accept *user input mid-run* with the script's ability to receive input — `args` covers that case.

questions.prompt: You want each saved run to write into a new folder named after the time it started, and you want a relaunch to be able to repeat the run. What is the right move?
options: Pass the timestamp in through `args` and let the script use it
Call `Date.now()` at the top of the script and format it
Call `new Date()` for the folder name and `Date.now()` for a log line
Add a `phase('timestamp')` call and read the time from it
questions.explanation: The runtime makes `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, and a no-argument `new Date()` throw, precisely so a relaunched run repeats the same `agent()` calls instead of silently diverging. That is why the first two tempting answers are wrong rather than merely inelegant — the calls do not return values, they fail. `phase()` is real but it groups agents under a title in the progress view; it carries no clock.

questions.prompt: You edit a saved workflow's `.js` file while a session is open, and run `/<name>` again. Nothing changes. What did you miss?
options: Run `/reload-skills` so the session re-reads the workflow directories, then run `/<name>` again
Delete the run from `/workflows` first, or the old script is reused
Re-save the workflow from `/workflows` so the edit is registered
Restart Claude Code; workflow files are read once at launch
questions.explanation: Saved workflows are files, and the session caches the directories it read; `/reload-skills` re-reads them, and then `/<name>` runs the edited version. `/workflows` manages running and completed runs, so deleting one has no bearing on which file a name resolves to — that is the most plausible wrong answer, because the runs list is where you normally touch workflows from the inside. Re-saving writes the *run's* script back to a location, which is the opposite direction. And a restart would eventually work, which is why it is tempting, but the documented step is the reload.
